subject: Physics
axis_note: ladder_position is a curriculum coordinate. It is never a learner estimate, and Core1A/Core1B may not consult one.

must_contain: normal and both media named before angles
one medium order preserved across index, angle and speed ratios

controlled_variation.notice: notice index and speed ratios invert together

must_contain: two normals and all i/r/e angle references shown

controlled_variation.hold: hold slab material and parallel faces
controlled_variation.notice: notice emergent direction remains parallel while lateral shift changes

must_contain: two independent principal rays agree on one image point

controlled_variation.hold: hold same lens and focal geometry
controlled_variation.notice: notice image nature, orientation and size change systematically

must_contain: optical centre and positive directions declared before signs

controlled_variation.notice: notice sign follows coordinate location, not image label

must_contain: signed u/v/f from one diagram and a ray-diagram cross-check

controlled_variation.vary: vary object distance in paraxial model
controlled_variation.hold: hold focal length and sign convention
controlled_variation.notice: notice equation image region tracks ray construction

must_contain: m = v/u and h_i/h_o interpreted for same image

controlled_variation.notice: notice sign and magnitude track orientation and relative size

must_contain: f converted to metres and sign retained before reciprocal

controlled_variation.notice: notice |P| changes inversely and sign tracks converging/diverging action

must_contain: safe distant object, sharp screen image, O-to-screen measurement and repeat check

controlled_variation.vary: vary object distance from far to farther
controlled_variation.notice: notice measured image distance approaches a stable focal-length estimate

family.invariant_demand: Translate normal-referenced refraction into an ordered medium/index model, build a consistent thin-lens ray picture and signed coordinate state, then connect image geometry to lens equation, magnification, power and the required practical interpretations.
family.difficult_move: Keeping medium order, principal-ray geometry and Cartesian signs consistent before substituting into any formula.
family.independent_check: Refraction direction, lens ray construction, signed formula result, magnification sign and practical observations must make compatible predictions.

support_ladder.handed_over: Normals, medium order, optical centre, focal points and positive coordinate directions are started.
The interface/lens geometry is labelled, but the learner chooses ratios, rays and signs.
Only the physical optical setup and requested quantity or practical outcome are supplied.

transfer.changed_demand: Use a thick lens or large-angle rays and decide whether the thin-lens paraxial formula remains adequate.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: whether the thin/paraxial approximation is satisfied

transfer.changed_demand: Convert between a lens ray diagram and signed u, v, f and m without changing the physical prediction.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: the coordinate signs implied by O, +x and +h

transfer.changed_demand: Explain why the emergent ray from a parallel glass slab can be parallel to the incident ray without being collinear.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: the second refraction restores direction but finite thickness permits lateral displacement

transfer.changed_demand: Explain why a distant-object convex-lens focal-length measurement is approximate and how to improve it.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: the role of finite object distance, alignment and repeated readings
